welcome:
Welcome to the sed & awk CLI Playground.
Type commands to explore text transformation on simulated config files and logs.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

steps.instruction: First, view the nginx config file we need to modify.
The listen port is wrong. Use sed to replace port 80 with 8080 (preview only, no file change).
Good. Now replace ALL occurrences of the old domain 'staging.example.com' with 'prod.example.com' globally.
We only want to see the server_name lines. Use sed to print only lines matching 'server_name'.
Delete all comment lines (lines starting with #) from the config to see just the directives.
Insert a new header 'X-Frame-Options DENY' after the line containing 'add_header X-Content-Type'.
steps.hint: Try: sed '/add_header X-Content-Type/a\    add_header X-Frame-Options DENY;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf

steps.instruction: Now chain multiple edits: replace the port AND the domain, then write in-place with a backup.
Verify the backup was created and diff the two files to confirm changes.

scenarios.title: Build a Log Analysis Pipeline with awk

steps.instruction: First, look at the raw access log to understand its format.
Print only the IP address (field 1) and HTTP status code (field 9) from each log line.
Filter the log to show only lines where the status code (field 9) is 500 or above.
Count total requests and errors using BEGIN/END blocks. Print a summary.
steps.expect: awk 'BEGIN{total=0; err=0} {total++; if($9>=500) err++} END{print "Total:", total, "Errors:", err, "Rate:", err/total*100 "%"}' /var/log/app/access.log
steps.hint: Try: awk 'BEGIN{total=0; err=0} {total++; if($9>=500) err++} END{print "Total:", total, "Errors:", err, "Rate:", err/total*100 "%"}' /var/log/app/access.log

steps.instruction: Use an associative array to count requests per HTTP status code and print the breakdown.
steps.expect: awk '{status[$9]++} END{for(s in status) print s, status[s]}' /var/log/app/access.log
steps.hint: Try: awk '{status[$9]++} END{for(s in status) print s, status[s]}' /var/log/app/access.log

steps.instruction: Find the top 5 IP addresses by request count. Pipe awk output through sort.
steps.expect: awk '{ips[$1]++} END{for(ip in ips) print ips[ip], ip}' /var/log/app/access.log | sort -rn | head -5
steps.hint: Try: awk '{ips[$1]++} END{for(ip in ips) print ips[ip], ip}' /var/log/app/access.log | sort -rn | head -5

steps.instruction: Now parse the CSV metrics file using a custom delimiter. Print service name and p99 latency.
Combine sed and awk: strip comment lines with sed, then sum the request_count column (field 3) with awk.
steps.hint: Try: sed '/^#/d' /var/log/app/metrics.csv | awk -F',' '{sum+=$3} END{print "Total requests:", sum}'

commands.help:
Available commands:

  sed 's/old/new/' file          — Substitute first match per line
  sed 's/old/new/g' file         — Substitute all matches per line
  sed -n '/pattern/p' file       — Print only matching lines
  sed -i[.bak] 'cmd' file       — Edit file in-place (with optional backup)
  sed '/pattern/d' file          — Delete matching lines
  sed '/pattern/a\text' file     — Append text after matching lines
  sed '/pattern/i\text' file     — Insert text before matching lines
  sed '5,10p' file               — Print lines 5 through 10
  sed -e 'cmd1' -e 'cmd2' file   — Chain multiple commands

  awk '{print}' file             — Print all lines (like cat)
  awk '{print $1, $3}' file      — Print specific fields
  awk -F',' '{print $1}' file    — Set field separator
  awk '/pattern/' file           — Filter lines by pattern
  awk 'BEGIN{...} {...} END{...}'— Init, per-line, summary blocks
  awk '{arr[$1]++} END{...}'     — Associative array aggregation
  awk '{printf fmt, args}' file  — Formatted output

  cat file                       — Display file contents
  head -N file                   — Show first N lines
  diff file1 file2               — Compare two files
  wc -l file                     — Count lines

  scenario                       — Start a guided lab
  clear                          — Clear the terminal
  help                           — Show this help
